phase3_findings.description: test_overlay_hint_opens_with_the_fallback_reason checks the warning tail on the memory-admin overlay but not on the table widget overlay.
Table harness records timer delays but no test asserts the flash duration; the no-warning 2500 ms case is untested.
Table widget shows the cancel/refusal message through the same flashMeta call as success, so it clears after 2.5 s and is not styled as an error.
Whole test module is skipped when node is not on PATH, so coverage reports as skipped rather than failed.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (suggestion-level findings and three inconclusive checklist items only)
The pull request is ready to merge: no reviewer or checklist item found a defect at or above the critical threshold, and every acceptance criterion was checked.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and inconclusive items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (5)

<details><summary>5 items</summary>

1. In `tests/unit/test_widget_export_outcomes.py` (lines 421-433), `test_overlay_hint_opens_with_the_fallback_reason` checks the warning tail on the memory-admin overlay but not on the table widget overlay, so a table overlay that dropped the formula-protection warning would still pass. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. In `tests/unit/test_widget_export_outcomes.py` (lines 336-341), the table harness records timer delays but no test asserts them, and every case carries a warning, so a regression in the 2500 ms flash duration for messages without a warning would go unnoticed. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. In `src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html`, the table widget shows "Download cancelled or blocked by the host." through the same `flashMeta` call as success, so without a warning it clears after 2.5 seconds and is not styled as an error, unlike memory admin's red banner. The criteria only require the red banner in memory admin. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. In `tests/unit/test_widget_export_outcomes.py` (line 267), the whole module is skipped when `node` is not on PATH, so a runner without node reports the acceptance coverage as skipped rather than failed. CI installs node, so this does not affect CI today. (raised by 1/5 agents)
- VC-14: FAIL (suggestion) — The memory-admin harness fakes showOk(message) and showError(title, message) with the same signatures as the real functions in memory_admin.html. [tests/unit/test_widget_export_outcomes.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tests/unit/test_widget_export_outcomes.py:108-109 defines showOk=(m)=>... (matches real showOk(message), memory_admin.html:507) and showError=(t,m)=>... but real showError is showError(title, message, details) (memory_admin.html:470, details rendered at 497-502). The export-failure path calls it with three args (memory_admin.html:1189: showError("Export failed ("+format+")", res.message, d.warnings || d)), so the fake silently drops details; signatures are not the same. showOk matches; showError does not.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

- VC-3: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The comment asserts the SDK's default request timeout is 60 s, which the 600000 ms override replaces. [src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html:378]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The comment at src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html:378-380 does claim a 60 s SDK default overridden by DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 600000. The @modelcontextprotocol/sdk shared/protocol source is not in the head view (grep for DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC found no matches), so the SDK's DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC could not be read. I did not check the SDK source or its published package. I recall the value being 60000 ms but recall is not evidence.

  </details>

- VC-7: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — A host cancel or refusal of ui/download-file resolves with `isError: true`; any other resolved result is treated as a successful save. [src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html:1110]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  memory_admin.html:1110-1115 does treat result.isError === true as cancel/refusal (red 'Export not saved') and any other resolved result as success, so the code matches the claim's description. The claim's source of truth is the MCP Apps / ext-apps SDK result schema for ui/download-file, which is not vendored in the head view (grep for download-file / McpUiDownloadFileResult finds only app code and the preview mock). I could not read the spec text confirming that cancel/denial resolves with isError: true, so I cannot confirm the contract. Missing evidence: the ext-apps SDK McpUiDownloadFileResult definition.

  </details>

- VC-8: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Hosts accept an embedded resource with a `file:///<name>` URI in ui/download-file contents and derive the saved filename from it. [src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html:414]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  query_results.html:408-420 sends contents:[{type:'resource',resource:{uri:'file:///query_results.csv',mimeType:'text/csv',text}}] (memory_admin.html:1099 uses the same shape with file:///<filename>). Whether hosts accept this and derive the saved filename from the URI is host/spec behavior (MCP Apps ui/download-file). The spec is not in the supplied artifacts, and the vendored SDK (app-with-deps.js lines 61 and 78) is minified into long lines the search tool omitted. The Read tool was not used on those lines. No other repo text states the filename-derivation rule. Missing evidence: the ext-apps spec/types for ui/download-file.

  </details>

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] In both widgets, on a host that does not advertise `downloadFile` and where a clipboard copy succeeds, the export copies the content and shows "This host can't save files — CSV copied to clipboard" in the table widget and "This host can't save files — Export copied to clipboard" in memory admin, with any warning tail appended.
- [ ] In both widgets, when `app.downloadFile` resolves with a result that does not have `isError: true` (an empty result included), the widget shows "Downloaded query_results.csv ✓" in the table widget and "Downloaded memory-export.json ✓" or "Downloaded memory-export.csv ✓" in memory admin, with any warning tail appended, and copies nothing.
- [ ] In both widgets, when `app.downloadFile` resolves with `isError: true`, the widget shows "Download cancelled or blocked by the host." with any warning tail appended (in memory admin, in the red error banner, never the green success banner), never shows a "Downloaded" message, does not write to the clipboard, and does not show the overlay.
- [ ] In both widgets, when `app.downloadFile` throws and a clipboard copy succeeds, the widget shows "Download failed (timed out) — CSV copied to clipboard" (memory admin: "Download failed (timed out) — Export copied to clipboard") for a thrown error whose `code` is -32001 (the SDK request timeout), and "Download failed (<the error's message>) — …" with the same ending for any other thrown error, in both cases with any warning tail appended.
- [ ] In both widgets, when the content reaches the overlay, the overlay hint opens with the same reason the clipboard message would have given ("This host can't save files" or "Download failed (<reason>)"), followed by "and the clipboard is blocked. Select all and copy:", and no longer says "Host blocked the file download".
- [ ] Both widgets call `app.downloadFile` with resource URI `file:///query_results.csv` (table widget) or `file:///memory-export.<json|csv>` (memory admin) and with request option `timeout: 600000`.
- [ ] Each widget's Export button label is unchanged whatever the host's capabilities.
- [ ] A node-run test covers each row of the Desired Behavior table, for the table widget (`exportCsv`) and for memory admin (`offerDownload`), at minimum: no capability with clipboard success; download resolving to an empty result; download resolving to `{isError: true}`; download throwing a timeout error; download throwing another error; no capability with both clipboard methods failing (overlay). `pytest -q` passes, and the existing check that warnings survive every export route in `tests/unit/test_output_boundaries.py` still passes.
- [ ] The change leaves host-side `downloadFile` support unchanged: on a host that does not advertise the capability, such as the tenant website chat widget if it does not, export still produces no file. A host-cancel and a host-refusal stay indistinguishable, because the SDK reports both as `isError: true`. A save dialog left open for more than 10 minutes still times out into the "Download failed (timed out)" clipboard route.
